step1.title: Download Data
step1.description: Downloads DFP (annual) and ITR (quarterly) financial statements from the CVM open data portal.

step2.title: Quality Filters
step2.description: Applies sequential filters to the raw CVM data across all financial statements (DRE, BPA, BPP, DFC): removes prior-year restated rows, filters to the selected company, resolves filing overlaps, and converts quarterly figures to standalone periods.
step2.dre_filter_desc: Keeps only income statement accounts — CD_CONTA codes starting with '3.'
step2.ordem_exerc_desc1: Keeps only the most recent exercise (ÚLTIMO) per filing
step2.holding_filter_desc: Excludes subsidiary holding entities to avoid double-counting
step2.company_selection_note: Selected {company} from {count} listed companies across 4 statement types (DRE, BPA, BPP, DFC)
step2.dfp_itr_overlap_desc: When annual (DFP) and quarterly (ITR) filings cover the same period, DFP takes precedence
step2.ytd_conversion_desc: Quarterly income statement and cash flow figures are reported as year-to-date cumulative. Converted to standalone quarters by subtracting the prior quarter.
step2.balance_sheet_note: Balance sheet data is not converted — it represents point-in-time snapshots.

step3.title: Statement Mapping
step3.description: Applies filing priority rules to the data from Step 2 — preferring annual filings (DFP) over quarterly (ITR), and standalone quarterly figures over YTD cumulative — then maps CVM account codes to a common financial model across income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow.

dedup_rules_list.description: When both an annual (DFP) and a quarterly (ITR) filing cover the same period and account, the annual filing takes priority. This prevents double-counting the same data at different granularities.

Q2 and Q3 ITR filings include two row sets: standalone quarterly figures (e.g., Apr–Jun) and YTD cumulative figures (e.g., Jan–Jun). Standalone rows are preferred; YTD rows are only kept when no standalone row exists for that period.
CVM filings report values in either UNIDADE (raw BRL) or MIL (thousands). All values are normalized to thousands (÷ 1000 where ESCALA_MOEDA = UNIDADE) before the accounts are pivoted into the model.

step4.title: Financial Metrics
step4.description: Computes derived financial metrics across profitability (margins, cost ratios), balance sheet health (liquidity, leverage, efficiency), and cash flow quality (free cash flow, capex intensity, earnings conversion).
step4.revenue_yoy_desc: Year-over-year change in net revenue. Positive = revenue grew vs prior year.
step4.cogs_yoy_desc: Year-over-year change in cost of goods sold (absolute value). Positive = costs increased vs prior year.
step4.gross_margin_desc: Gross profit as % of revenue = (Revenue − COGS) / Revenue. Measures production efficiency.
step4.ebit_margin_desc: Earnings before interest and taxes as % of revenue. Measures operating profitability before financing costs.
step4.ebitda_margin_desc: EBIT plus depreciation & amortization as % of revenue. Proxy for operating cash generation.
step4.cogs_revenue_desc: Cost of goods sold as % of revenue. Rising values indicate cost pressure or declining pricing power.
step4.sga_revenue_desc: Selling, general & administrative expenses as % of revenue. Measures overhead efficiency.
step4.bs_unavailable: Balance sheet data not available for this company.
step4.roe_clipped_note: Values clipped to -100% / +100% — actual range: {min}% to {max}%
step4.cf_unavailable: Cash flow data not available for this company.
step4.debt_to_ebitda_desc: Net debt divided by EBITDA. Measures how many years of operating earnings it would take to repay debt. Above 4× signals elevated leverage.
step4.current_ratio_desc: Current assets divided by current liabilities. A ratio above 1× means short-term assets cover short-term obligations.
step4.quick_ratio_desc: Current assets minus inventories, divided by current liabilities. A stricter liquidity test that excludes hard-to-liquidate inventory.
step4.return_on_assets_desc: Net income as a percentage of total assets. Measures how efficiently the company generates profit from its asset base.
step4.return_on_equity_desc: Net income as a percentage of shareholders' equity. Measures the return delivered to equity holders.
step4.net_debt_brlm_desc: Total debt (short-term + long-term) minus cash and equivalents. Positive = net borrower; negative = net cash position.
step4.ocf_desc: Cash generated from core operating activities before investing or financing. The primary measure of earnings quality.
step4.fcf_brlm_desc: Operating cash flow minus capital expenditures. Cash available for debt repayment, dividends, and growth after maintaining assets.
step4.ocf_to_ni_desc: Operating cash flow divided by net income. Values above 1× indicate earnings are backed by real cash; below 1× flags accruals risk.
step4.capex_to_revenue_desc: Capital expenditures as a percentage of revenue. Reflects asset intensity and the company's investment cycle stage.

step5.title: Metric Validation
step5.description: Confirms the computed financial metrics are trustworthy before running pattern detection. Validates plausibility bounds across profitability, balance sheet, and cash flow metrics, and checks cross-statement consistency.
step5.bounds_default_note: Using default bounds — sector-specific analysis unavailable

bounds.rationale: Values outside this range suggest raw data errors or extreme non-recurring items — petrochemical gross margins rarely exceed 80% or fall below -50%.
EBIT below -50% typically indicates large impairments rather than operating losses; above 60% is implausible for asset-heavy industrials.
COGS below 20% of revenue is unrealistic for commodity manufacturers; above 130% flags a data scaling or sign error.
SG&A above 40% of revenue is implausible for industrial companies and likely reflects a misclassified cost line.

bs_bounds.rationale: Below 0.1× suggests a data error; above 10× is implausible for capital-intensive companies.
Negative values occur with negative EBITDA; above 30× suggests near-zero EBITDA or a data error.
Informational: flags a net cash position (net_debt < 0). Not an error — indicates the company holds more cash than debt.
Year-over-year swings above 200% suggest a data anomaly or a significant structural event.
Above 5× is implausible for asset-heavy industrial companies; below 0 indicates negative revenue.
Values outside this range suggest data scaling errors or extreme non-recurring items.
Extreme values are mathematically possible with small equity but flag for review.

cf_bounds.rationale: Values outside this range suggest extreme non-cash adjustments or data inconsistency between statements.
Capex above 50% of revenue is implausible even for the most capital-intensive industries.
Above 5× suggests a major expansion phase or a data error in depreciation figures.
Free cash flow exceeding revenue in absolute terms (positive or negative) flags a data anomaly.

step5.cross_note_cash_reconciliation: Consistent gaps across all periods suggest a systematic cause such as FX translation effects on foreign-currency cash balances, or restricted cash items not captured in the three-line cash flow summary.
step5.cross_note_da_consistency: Minor differences between income statement and cash flow D&A values are common due to rounding or line-item classification differences.
step5.cross_note_balance_sheet_equation: Any imbalance indicates a potential account mapping error in the data pipeline and should be investigated.
